summary: I closed the two open review fixes, O-024 and O-025, and changed nothing else. For O-024, the stall Fact now lists 'stall' a second time after its assertions, on a background thread through the same DirectoryReader the scan uses, and leaves that listing blocked. SyncRootRig.Dispose kills the provider with this process's request pending, which is the path spike 4's kill arm measured, and fails the Fact if the kill does not free the listing within 10 s. Before every kill, Dispose writes a 'teardown shape: PENDING | none pending' line with this process's FETCH_PLACEHOLDERS and CANCEL_FETCH_PLACEHOLDERS counts and everything the provider printed, so each passing run records which shape it tore down. For O-025, the sweep test now includes a junction named like a dead run's root, pointing outside the swept folder. A mutation run showed the test fails when the sweep's LinkTarget guard is removed. The default suite still passes (332, no gated test run). The stall Fact itself is still unrun, because open question 1 is unanswered.

files.why: O-024. After its assertions the stall Fact calls rig.HoldListing("stall", 10 s) and logs whether a fresh FETCH_PLACEHOLDERS came from this pid. New in SyncRootRig: HoldListing and HeldListing, and IsOwnCallback, now shared with WaitForCallback. WaitForLine gains 'from' and 'stop'. ShapeAtKill writes the 'teardown shape:' line. Before the kill, Dispose writes that line plus Captured(); after the kill it joins any held listing for up to 10 s and logs how many ms after the provider exited it returned, or records a teardown failure. The class and rig remarks describe this.

O-025. TheSweepRemovesOnlyTheRootOfARunThatIsGone adds tree.Junction(CloudRig.RootName(gone, Guid.NewGuid()), tree.Outside("target")) with not-ours.txt in the target. It asserts the junction is in neither swept nor unregistered, that the junction still exists, and that the target's file still exists.

obligations.how: Done in three parts. (1) Before the kill, Dispose writes 'teardown shape: PENDING …' or 'teardown shape: none pending …', with this pid's FETCH_PLACEHOLDERS and CANCEL_FETCH_PLACEHOLDERS counts, the state of any held listing, and all of Captured(). I saw these lines on the two non-registering gated Facts. (2) This corrects my attempt-1 O-006 account, which was wrong. On the stall Fact's passing path, cts.Cancel() frees the scan's listing and the request can be withdrawn (the provider reports CANCEL_FETCH_PLACEHOLDERS) before Dispose kills the provider. Nothing in attempt 1 fed or observed a request pending at the kill. (3) After its assertions and without adding a third Fact, the stall Fact now lists stall again on a background thread and waits up to 10 s for a fresh FETCH_PLACEHOLDERS from this pid. Dispose then kills the provider with that listing blocked, and a teardown failure is raised if the listing is not freed within 10 s. As the disposition allows, the fresh request is logged, not asserted: no spike measured a second listing after a cancelled one. If it never arrives, the output says 'none pending'. This all compiles and the logging path ran. The PENDING path itself has not run on a real sync root, because open question 1 is unanswered.

TheSweepRemovesOnlyTheRootOfARunThatIsGone now makes a junction named CloudRig.RootName(gone, Guid.NewGuid()) that points at tree.Outside("target"), with not-ours.txt inside. It asserts the junction is in neither swept nor unregistered, that it still exists, and that the target's file still exists. The test passes. With CloudRig.Sweep's `LinkTarget is not null` guard removed it failed: swept contained both the stale root and the junction. I restored the guard, and CloudRig.cs matches HEAD again.

Each teardown wrote, for example, 'teardown shape: none pending, no request of this process is known to be pending at the kill; the provider had already exited (2); this process raised 0 FETCH_PLACEHOLDERS and 0 CANCEL_FETCH_PLACEHOLDERS; the test held no listing', followed by the provider's stdout and stderr. Teardown took 1-4 ms, with no fsa-cf-* left.
Default run: 332 passed, 0 failed. The trx shows 0 CloudPlaceholderTests, StalledShareTests or TEST-NET-1 tests executed.

tests.note: It registers a real cldflt sync root, and design open question 1 (may that happen on this PC) is still open in the slice index. So the held listing, the PENDING teardown shape and the kill freeing it within 10 s have compiled but never run on a real root. Validate, if the person allows it, reads the 'teardown shape:' line in each of its three runs.

follow_ups: If open question 1 is answered yes, validate runs the opt-in filter three times in a row. In each run it reads the stall Fact's 'teardown shape:' line (PENDING or none pending) and 'the held listing of stall returned N ms after the provider was gone'. That is the first real evidence for C-006. If a second listing after a cancelled one raises no fresh FETCH_PLACEHOLDERS, the line says 'none pending', and C-006's shape needs another way in.

The follow-ups from attempt 1 still stand: the RuleCases.ps1 pin of 28 settled entries (HEAD had 32 before this slice), rules-harness cross-engine agreement, and the unmeasured case of a kill freeing a pending FETCH_DATA.
